budget.comment: Auto-prompting's real failure mode is becoming nagware and getting switched off wholesale. The budget is what keeps the feature alive: at most two ambient offers per session, and a dismissed trigger goes quiet for a day.

triggers.fires: Load prior context for this project (/wiki-pull) and state the current stage plus the single next step.
triggers.why: rules/skill-router.md says every research session should start with /wiki-pull. That was a hope; a hook makes it real. RE-DISABLED 2026-08-12 after the plugin sync silently reverted this to true, which would have duplicated wiki-context.py's own SessionStart digest.

triggers.fires: Open the NEXT stage's interview instead of waiting to be asked (discovery -> /strategize, strategy -> /analyze, analysis -> /write, writing -> /peer-review).
triggers.why: The pipeline knows what comes next. Making the user remember the command is the friction.

triggers.fires: Socratic decision-record beat: what did you decide, what did you reject, what would invalidate it.
triggers.why: A stage passes and the reasoning evaporates. Decision records are cheap now and irreplaceable at revision time.

triggers.fires: Explain what this code does at the level of an economics student - define jargon, no assumed familiarity - before moving on.
triggers.why: _brain/profile.md mandates that all code Claude writes be explained so the user learns alongside. That currently depends on Claude remembering.

triggers.fires: Before patching: ask what the user thinks the fix is. Semi-autonomous means plan together, then execute.
triggers.why: profile.md asks for Socratic planning then execution. Silently patching a critic finding skips the half the user asked for.

triggers.fires: Offer /learn on that concept - a curriculum beats re-explaining it next month.
triggers.why: Repeated clarification is the signal Engram exists to catch, and it is currently invisible.

triggers.fires: Surface the due count and offer /recall.
triggers.why: Already shipped. Listed here so the registry is the complete picture, not a partial one.

triggers.fires: Remind once per session to run /wiki-push.

triggers.condition: git status --porcelain is nonempty in the project dir (works identically for BMAD projects with no passport.yaml)
triggers.fires: Offer the session-close ritual (git-workflow -> checkpoint -> wiki-push), matching the phd-session-close procedure.
triggers.why: The audit's top-scored real gap: 'checkpoint every session with work'. Evidenced verbatim in a real session (Job Insecurity, mined 2026-08-12): the exact three-skill ritual, in that order, on explicit command -- nothing previously reminded the user to run it.
